nm_05_health_wall.blurb: A compact wall of fifteen routes on the Original Side at Mentmore, in the Gallup area. Most lines are bolted sport climbs, with a handful of gear routes and one that is commonly top-roped. Difficulty starts at 5.7 and tops out in the 5.12s, with the biggest share in the 5.10s and a healthy group of 5.11s and 5.12s for stronger climbers. The wall sits at the east end of the crag, with a big overhang at its right end and a prominent arete separating it from the neighbouring Benny Silva wall. The stone is sandstone. A good stop for a mixed-ability party that wants a bit of everything.
nm_05_health_wall.approach: From the parking area, drop down through the arroyo to the original side of the crag. The trail normally arrives between this wall and the Benny Silva wall next to it.

nm_unbeatable_boulder.blurb: A lone boulder standing by itself in open ground in the Southern Box, part of the bouldering near Socorro, and easy to pick out from the Major Wall parking. It holds fifteen problems on rhyolite, from VB-level slabs up to V9. About half fall between V0 and V2, a few sit at V4 and V5, and the hardest lines are eliminates. Two sides have vertical faces and the north side is steep, with a tree behind it. Because it stands in the open, it takes the weather fully, so it can be warm in winter sun and punishing in summer heat.

nm_beer_block.blurb: A single block within the El Rito sport area, near El Rito in northern New Mexico, carrying fifteen bolted routes on conglomerate cobble rock. There is nothing easy here: the lines run from 5.11 into 5.13, and most are 5.12, so it suits climbers already comfortable on steep, hard sport routes. The cobbles and the pockets they leave behind make the holds, and some of the lines are on the block's north side, so it stays cooler than the sunnier walls nearby. Expect short, punchy climbs rather than long pitches.

nm_john_s_wall.blurb: A small basalt wall right beside the dirt road at the John Dunn Bridge area near Taos, close to where the Rio Hondo meets the Rio Grande. It is the oldest and easiest-to-reach wall in the gorge, with fifteen routes: nine trad and six sport, from 5.7 up to 5.13. Most of the grades fall between 5.8 and 5.11, so there is plenty for moderate leaders. It faces south, making it one of the warmest winter spots around and a hot place in summer. Fixed gear can be old, with worn chains and loose rock in places, so check what you clip.

nm_rad_wall.blurb: The steepest wall in the El Rito sport area, near El Rito in northern New Mexico, with fifteen bolted sport routes on conglomerate. The cliff is steep to overhanging throughout, and the routes are long and sustained, with plenty of pockets formed by cobbles in the rock. Most lines are 5.12, with a few 5.9s and 5.10s and a 5.7 for warming up, so it is mainly a destination for strong sport climbers. The bolting is sensible rather than excessive, and a stick-clip can help on the first clip. A large ponderosa pine marks the right end of the wall.

nm_boulder_36.blurb: A large boulder topped by a chockstone, sitting beside a campsite at Aguirre Springs on the east side of the Organ Mountains near Las Cruces. It has room for a good number of lines, and fifteen problems are recorded. The grades are friendly: twelve are V0 to V2, with a single V3, a V4, and one V7 for the strong. That makes it a handy spot for beginners, warm-ups and short sessions when you want to hop between a few easy problems without a long hike.
